481.h: Minaret University (MU) is a private university established by the Ahmadiyya Muslim Jama'at of Nigeria, under the leadership of Alhaji Alatoye Folorunso AbdulAzeez. The National Universities Commission records its establishment in 2025. It was created to address gaps in education in agriculture, science and technology, and to produce graduates who create jobs.
481.a: The university emphasises entrepreneurial, practical education, using hands-on training and a work-study approach, with programmes concentrated in agriculture, science and technology.
481.c: It is located in Ikirun, Osun State.

485.h: Monarch University is a private Christian university that received its Federal Government licence through the National Universities Commission in 2025.
485.a: The university offers 14 undergraduate programmes in two faculties: Humanities, Management and Social Sciences; and Basic and Applied Sciences. Its leadership includes Professor Omoegun, a former Dean of Education at the University of Lagos and pioneer Dean of Education at Ajayi Crowther University.
485.c: It is located in Iyesi-Ota, Ogun State.

493.h: Greenland University, Jalingo (GLU) is a private university licensed by the National Universities Commission in 2025. It was founded with the aim of becoming an entrepreneurial university that turns out job creators rather than job seekers, and its motto is 'Knowledge for Self Reliance'. It draws students from every geopolitical zone of Nigeria.
493.a: The university offers undergraduate programmes built around entrepreneurship. Its football academy combines player development with education.
493.c: It is located in Jalingo, the capital of Taraba State.

495.h: Azione Verde University is a private university established by Opera Don Bonifacio Azione Verde, a humanitarian organisation founded in 2002. It responded to the Federal Government's invitation for private investment in higher education, and received approval as one of nine new private universities; the National Universities Commission records 2025. It aims to combine academic standards with moral, social and spiritual values.
495.c: It is located in Amaigbo, Imo State.

501.h: Bayelsa Medical University (BMU) is a public university specialising in medicine and the health sciences. It was created by the Bayelsa Medical University Law, passed by the state House of Assembly in 2018, and established in 2019 under Governor Seriake Dickson to address shortages of health workers in the Niger Delta and the rest of Nigeria.
501.a: BMU began with two pioneer faculties, including Basic Medical Sciences, and trains doctors and other health professionals across medicine and the allied medical sciences.
501.c: It is located in Yenagoa, the capital of Bayelsa State.

502.h: Dennis Osadebay University, Asaba is a public university, one of three new universities set up by the Delta State Government and approved by the National Universities Commission in 2021. It is named after Dennis Osadebay, premier of the former Mid-Western Region.
502.a: The university offers four- and five-year bachelor's degrees in eight faculties, with more than 73 accredited courses. Full-time undergraduate admission is only through JAMB's UTME or direct entry, with five O-level credits as required by each department.
502.c: It is located in Asaba, the capital of Delta State.

504.h: Kingsley Ozumba Mbadiwe University (KOMU), formerly Eastern Palm University, is a public university owned by the Imo State Government. It is named after Kingsley Ozumba Mbadiwe, the nationalist politician. The National Universities Commission records its establishment in 2016.
504.a: KOMU has nine faculties and 34 departments, ranging from computing and law to medicine and surgery. It accepts inter-university and internal transfer applications.
504.c: It is located at Ogboko, in Ideato South local government area of Imo State.
